To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) personality assessment in Great Apes can be based on three methods: behavior measures, behavior rating, and adjective rating; (2) behavior ratings are most reliable, temporally-stable, and show the strongest cross-method coherence; (3) behavior ratings are best at predicting behavior measures; (4) behavior ratings are better predictors than adjective ratings; (5) personality constructs can be derived from the species’ behavior repertoire, but (6) the trait structure of Great Apes differs from

the personality traits of the Great Apes were reliably measured by behavior measures, behavior and adjective ratings, and that behavior ratings were more closely related to behavior measures than were adjective ratings.
(1) the personality structure of the four studied Great Apes is similar and (2) personality assessment in the Great apes should be based on behavior ratings.
